'''Robert K. Colwell''' is an American evolutionary ecologist, biogeographer, biodiversity scientist, and tropical biologist.<ref name="esa">{{cite web |title=Distinguished Service Citation |website=Ecological Society of America (ESA) |url=https://esa.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/94/2022/02/service1999.pdf |access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref> He is Board of Trustees Distinguished Professor Emeritus in the Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at the [[University of Connecticut]] and Museum Curator Adjoint in Entomology and Zoology at the [[University of Colorado Boulder|University of Colorado]] Museum of Natural History.<ref name="cv2025">{{cite web |last=Colwell |first=Robert K. |title=Curriculum Vitae |date=2025 |url=https://spaces-cdn.owlstown.com/blobs/zh6njle4vw45rqfv7x66hmnvaxqc |format=PDF |access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref><ref name="colorado">{{cite web |title=Dr. Robert Colwell |website=University of Colorado Boulder |url=https://www.colorado.edu/cumuseum/dr-robert-colwell |access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref> An expert in biodiversity statistics, Colwell is a developer of methods for estimating species richness from incomplete data and is best known for the mid-domain effect and for inventing and developing widely-used software tools in biodiversity informatics.<ref name="amacad">{{cite web |title=Robert K. Colwell |website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |date=13 February 2026 |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/robert-k-colwell |access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title=EstimateS turns 20: Statistical estimation of species richness and shared species from samples, with non-parametric extrapolation {{!}} Request PDF |url=https://nsojournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1111/ecog.00814 |archive-url= |archive-date= |access-date=2026-03-11 |website=Wiley Online Library |doi=10.1111/ecog.00814 |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Colwell is the younger of two children of Robert Pulliam Colwell,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2004-10-12 |title=Robert Colwell Obituary |url=https://www.denverpost.com/obituaries/robert-pulliam-colwell-co/ |access-date=2026-03-11 |website=The Denver Post |language=en-US}}</ref> a public-school principal and rancher, and Eleanor Knight Colwell,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-03-05 |title=Eleanor Colwell Obituary |url=https://www.denverpost.com/obituaries/eleanor-k-colwell-co/ |access-date=2026-03-11 |website=The Denver Post |language=en-US}}</ref> a concert flutist and amateur naturalist.<ref name="cv2025" /> He attended public schools in Denver, but his interest in biology was kindled by weekends and summers on the family cattle ranch in the mountains.<ref name="cv2025" /> Colwell was married to writer and poet [[Mary Mackey]] from 1965 to 1972. He subsequently married geneticist [[Mary-Claire King]] in 1973; the marriage ended in 1983. In 1985, he married [[Robin Chazdon]]

In 1965, Colwell received a Bachelor of Arts (AB) degree from [[Harvard University]].<ref name="cv2025" /><ref name="weiss2011">{{cite web |last=Weiss |first=Cindy |title=Colwell Elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences |website=UConn Today |date=2011-04-20 |url=https://today.uconn.edu/2011/04/colwell-elected-to-american-academy-of-arts-and-sciences/ |access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref> In 1966, he worked as a curatorial assistant in ethnobotany under [[Richard Evans Schultes]] at Harvard.<ref name="cv2025" /> In 1969, he received his Ph.D. in Ecology from the [[University of Michigan]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-07-16 |title=Robert K. Colwell |url=https://theconversation.com/profiles/robert-k-colwell-517529 |access-date=2026-03-11 |website=The Conversation |language=en-US}}</ref> under the supervision of [[Lawrence Slobodkin]].<ref name="cv2025" /><ref name="slobodkin2011">{{cite journal |last1=Futuyma |first1=Douglas J. |last2=Colwell |first2=Robert K. |title=Resolution of Respect: Lawrence B. Slobodkin 1928–2009 |journal=Bulletin of the Ecological Society of America |year=2011 |volume=92 |issue=1 |pages=19–26 |doi=10.1890/0012-9623-92.1.19 |bibcode=2011BuESA..92...19C }}</ref> He was a Ford Foundation Fellow at the [[University of Chicago]] from 1969 to 1970, working with Monte Lloyd and [[Richard Levins]].<ref name="cv2025" />

==Career==
Colwell served on the faculty of the Department of Zoology at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 1970 to 1989.<ref name="cv2025" /> In 1989, he joined the faculty of the Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at the University of Connecticut, where he was named a Board of Trustees Distinguished Professor in 2001.<ref name="boardoftrustees">{{Cite web |title=University of Connecticut Office of the Provost {{!}} The Board of Trustees Distinguished Professor Award |date=17 December 2021 |url=https://provost.uconn.edu/awards-honors/the-board-of-trustees-distinguished-professor-award/ |access-date=2026-03-11 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="weiss2011" /> After retiring from teaching in 2014, he became a Distinguished Research Professor at the University of Connecticut.<ref name="cv2025" /> He also holds a position as Curator Adjoint of Entomology and Zoology at the University of Colorado Museum of Natural History.<ref name="cv2025" /><ref name="colorado" /> Since 2010, he has been an International Collaborator at the Center for Macroecology, Evolution and Climate at the University of Copenhagen, and from 2014 to 2025 he was Professor e Pesquisador Visitante Especial, Universidade Federal de Goiás, Brazil.<ref name="cv2025" /><ref>{{cite web |title=People |website=University of Copenhagen (Center for Macroecology, Evolution and Climate) |date=August 2022 |url=https://macroecology.ku.dk/people/ |access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=UFG tem dois professores entre os mais influentes do mundo |url=https://ufg.br/n/112080-ufg-tem-dois-professores-entre-os-mais-influentes-do-mundo |access-date=2026-03-11 |website=UFG - Universidade Federal de Goiás |language=pt-BR}}</ref>

==Other professional work==
Colwell served on the Board of Reviewing Editors of the journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' from 2002 to 2005.<ref name="cv2025" /> He has been Editor-in-Chief for Reviews and Syntheses for the journal ''[[Ecography (journal)|Ecography]]'' since 2014<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editorial Board |url=https://www.ecography.org/about-journal/editorial-board |access-date=2026-03-11 |website=www.ecography.org |language=en}}</ref> and has served in various editorial roles for other journals.<ref name="cv2025" /> He was also an Associate Editor for the ''[https://www.sciencedirect.com/referencework/9780122268656/encyclopedia-of-biodiversity Encyclopedia of Biodiversity]'' between 1999 and 2012.<ref name="cv2025" />

In the 1980s and 1990s, Colwell advised several public agencies, including the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency|U.S. Environmental Protection Agency]] (EPA), the [[National Institutes of Health]] (NIH), the [[United States Department of Agriculture]] (USDA), and the [[Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development]] (OECD).<ref name="cv2025" /><ref name="amacad" /> His work during this period focused on the environmental, ecological, and evolutionary risks associated with genetically engineered organisms.<ref name="cv2025" />

==Research==
The central theme of Colwell's research is biological diversity, from the coexistence and coevolution of species within ecological communities to the origin, diversification, and evolutionary adaptation of species across geographical and geological timescales.<ref name="amacad" /> His work has contributed to advances in process-based simulation of biogeography, global-change biogeography, biodiversity statistics, biodiversity inventory, and biodiversity informatics.<ref name="amacad" />

===Key areas of contribution===

* '''Biogeographical null models.''' With co-author David Winkler, Colwell developed one of the first biogeographical null models incorporating simulated evolutionary diversification and stochastic dispersal.<ref name="cv2025" /><ref name="colwellwinkler1984">{{cite book |last1=Colwell |first1=Robert K. |last2=Winkler |first2=David W. |chapter=A null model for null models in biogeography |title=Ecological Communities: Conceptual Issues and the Evidence |editor1-last=Strong |editor1-first=Donald R. |editor2-last=Simberloff |editor2-first=Daniel |editor3-last=Abele |editor3-first=Lawrence G. |editor4-last=Thistle |editor4-first=Anne B. |publisher=Princeton University Press |location=Princeton |year=1984 |pages=344–359 |doi=10.1515/9781400857081.344 |isbn=978-1-4008-5708-1 }}</ref>
* '''The mid-domain effect (MDE).''' With George Hurtt, Colwell demonstrated that species diversity may peak in the center of bounded geographical domains when species ranges are randomly distributed.<ref name="mde2000">{{cite journal |last1=Colwell |first1=Robert K. |last2=Lees |first2=David C. |title=The mid-domain effect: geometric constraints on the geography of species richness |journal=Trends in Ecology & Evolution |year=2000 |volume=15 |issue=2 |pages=70–76 |doi=10.1016/S0169-5347(99)01767-X}}</ref><ref name="colwellhurtt1994">{{cite journal |last1=Colwell |first1=Robert K. |last2=Hurtt |first2=George C. |title=Nonbiological gradients in species richness and a spurious Rapoport effect |journal=The American Naturalist |year=1994 |volume=144 |issue=4 |pages=570–595 |doi=10.1086/285695 |bibcode=1994ANat..144..570C }}</ref>
* '''Biodiversity statistics.''' Colwell collaborated extensively with Jonathan Coddington, [[Anne Chao]], and Nicholas Gotelli to develop statistical methods for estimating species richness from sampling data.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gotelli |first1=Nicholas J. |last2=Colwell |first2=Robert K. |title=Quantifying biodiversity: procedures and pitfalls in the measurement and comparison of species richness |journal=Ecology Letters |year=2001 |volume=4 |issue=4 |pages=379–391 |doi=10.1046/j.1461-0248.2001.00230.x |bibcode=2001EcolL...4..379G }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chao |first1=Anne |last2=Gotelli |first2=Nicholas J. |last3=Hsieh |first3=Tracy C. |last4=Sander |first4=Elizabeth L. |last5=Ma |first5=K. H. |last6=Colwell |first6=Robert K. |last7=Ellison |first7=Aaron M. |title=Rarefaction and extrapolation with Hill numbers: a framework for sampling and estimation in species diversity studies |journal=Ecological Monographs |year=2014 |volume=84 |issue=1 |pages=45–67 |doi=10.1890/13-0133.1 |bibcode=2014EcoM...84...45C |url=http://nrs.harvard.edu/urn-3:HUL.InstRepos:11148822 }}</ref>
* '''Biodiversity informatics.''' He co-directed Project ALAS, a long-term tropical arthropod diversity inventory in Costa Rica and developed the biodiversity database software ''Biota''.<ref name="amacad" /><ref name="alas">{{cite web |last1=Colwell |first1=Robert K. |last2=Longino |first2=John T. |title=Project ALAS: Arthropods of La Selva |url=http://viceroy.eeb.uconn.edu/ALAS/ |access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref><ref name="biota">{{cite web |last=Colwell |first=Robert K. |title=Biota: The Biodiversity Database Manager |website=Robert K. Colwell Academic Website |url=https://www.robertkcolwell.org/pages/1414-biota |access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref>
* '''Climate-driven range shifts.''' In 2008, Colwell and colleagues published research predicting upslope range shifts of tropical species under climate warming and lowland biotic attrition.<ref name="colwell2008">{{cite journal |last1=Colwell |first1=Robert K. |last2=Brehm |first2=Gunnar |last3=Cardelús |first3=Catherine L. |last4=Gilman |first4=Alex C. |last5=Longino |first5=John T. |title=Global warming, elevational range shifts, and lowland biotic attrition in the wet tropics |journal=Science |year=2008 |volume=322 |issue=5899 |pages=258–261 |doi=10.1126/science.1162547 |bibcode=2008Sci...322..258C }}</ref><ref name="weiss2011" />
* '''Hummingbird flower mites.''' Colwell conducted research on mites that live in hummingbird-pollinated flowers, compete with hummingbirds for nectar, and disperse between plants in the nostrils of the birds, contributing to knowledge of coevolution, sexual selection for host fidelity, and community ecology.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Colwell |first=Robert K. |title=Competition for the nectar of ''Centropogon valerii'' by the hummingbird ''Colibri thalassinus'' and the flower-piercer ''Diglossa plumbea'', and its evolutionary implications |journal=The Condor |year=1974 |volume=76 |issue=4 |pages=447–452 |doi=10.2307/1366346 |jstor=1366346 |url=https://digitalcommons.usf.edu/condor/vol76/iss3/11 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Colwell |first=Robert K. |title=Competition and coexistence in a simple tropical community |journal=The American Naturalist |year=1973 |volume=107 |issue=958 |pages=737–760 |doi=10.1086/282872 |bibcode=1973ANat..107..737C }}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
Colwell has received numerous professional honors. He served as President of the American Society of Naturalists in 1998 <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amnat.org/about/history/past-ec.html|title=Past Officers of the ASN}}</ref> and received the President's Award from the society in 2001.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amnat.org/awards.html|title=Awards|website=www.amnat.org}}</ref> He was Vice President of the Ecological Society of America from 1994 to 1995 and received the ESA Distinguished Service Award in 1999.<ref name="esa" /><ref>{{cite journal |title=Officers of the Ecological Society of America |website=JSTOR |jstor=20168018 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/20168018 |access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref> He was elected Fellow of the Ecological Society of America in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://esa.org/about/awards/fellows-program/esa-fellows | title=ESA Fellows | website=esa.org}}</ref>

He is also a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science, the California Academy of Sciences, and the Connecticut Academy of Science and Engineering.<ref name="cv2025" /> In 2011 he was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.<ref name="amacad" /><ref name="weiss2011" /> In 2018 and 2025, he was named a Clarivate Highly Cited Researcher.<ref name="cv2025" />

The mite species ''Tropicoseius'' (''Rhinoseius'') ''colwelli'' Hunter 1972, the katydid species ''Acantheremus colwelli'' Naskrecki 1997 (Colwell's Horned Katydid), and the ant species ''Lenomyrmex colwelli'' Longino 2006 were named to honor Colwell.<ref>{{cite web |title=Treatment: Acantheremus colwelli Naskrecki, 1997 |website=Plazi |url=https://plazi.org/treatment?id=FFB3F15CD91CFFD62BA6F846C317D408 |access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Lenomyrmex colwelli Longino, 2006 |website=AntCat |url=https://antcat.org/catalog/476928 |access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Fain |first=Alex |title=Notes on the genus Rhinoseius Baker & Yunker, 1964 (Acari: Ascidae) III. Rhinoseius and allied genera of Costa Rica and Panama |journal=Bulletin et Annales de la Société Royale Belge d'Entomologie |year=1992 |url=https://www.revues.uliege.be/cipletinsectes/article/download/1018/786 |access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref>
